concerns.text: The plan validates the verifier’s alignment scores against 'human‑annotated feasibility scores' (FR‑001, FR‑003), yet these scores are *synthetically* generated via a deterministic antonym‑lookup procedure (see research.md §2). Because the same lexical resources and rule‑based logic underpin both the synthetic human scores and the symbolic constraint‑graph parser (which also uses an antonym lexicon to detect contradictions), the validation target is not independent of the predictor. This creates a circular/tautological validation: improvement in verifier scores may simply reflect alignment with the same rule‑based metric used to construct the graphs, not genuine model improvement.

Section 2 labels the generated scores as 'human feasibility scores' but they are algorithmically derived, not obtained from actual human annotators. This mischaracterisation undermines the claim of measuring alignment with true human judgments and violates the methodological requirement that ground‑truth labels be independent and empirically obtained.

The statistical comparison (paired t‑test or Wilcoxon) tests the difference between baseline and graph‑augmented verifier scores *relative to the same synthetic human_score*. Since the human_score is deterministic and derived from the same rule‑based system that produces the graphs, the test does not assess whether the graph augmentation genuinely improves alignment with external reality; it merely measures consistency with an internally generated metric.
